candidates.attacker_control: An unauthenticated client fully controls the ID and filter parameters sent to the public /controlledvocabulary servlet (mapped in web.xml lines 756-759; servlet definition lines 423-426) or directly to /controlledvocabulary/controlledvocabulary.jsp. Values are copied verbatim into the HTTP session and then emitted unencoded into the response. No login, CSRF token or prior session state is required.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Verified the values are not sanitized at insertion: no StringEscapeUtils/Utils.addEntities/ESAPI encoding is applied in controlledvocabulary.jsp, unlike its sibling controlledvocabulary/search.jsp (line 56) and unlike other JSPUI pages (feedback/form.jsp, search/advanced.jsp, suggest/suggest.jsp). Verified the endpoints are not protected by web.xml security constraints or by the admin-only/registered-only filter mappings (web.xml lines 73-117). Verified the sink is a genuine HTML/script context (contentType text/html; script element at lines 43-74). Considered that the ID sink sits inside a JS function that normally runs on user click, but the </script> breakout executes at parse time, so function timing does not prevent exploitation. Could not execute the application, and could not diff against upstream to confirm whether this was later patched. No runtime confirmation.
candidates.impact: Reflected cross-site scripting executing in the DSpace web application origin with the victim session. This allows arbitrary in-origin JavaScript: performing actions as the victim, reading/altering page content and tokens, exfiltrating data, and phishing. Because ID/filter are also persisted in the session, the payload can be re-triggered on later requests of the same session.
candidates.prerequisites: Victim must follow a crafted link to the JSPUI deployment (standard reflected-XSS delivery). Endpoints are unprotected: web.xml has no security-constraint, and filter mappings cover only /dspace-admin/* (admin-only) and /mydspace, /tools/*, /profile, /submit, /subscribe, /workspace, /view-workspaceitem (registered-only), leaving /controlledvocabulary and /controlledvocabulary/* unfiltered. The page is served as text/html (page directive line 18).
candidates.root_cause: controlledvocabulary.jsp writes user-controlled values into HTML/JavaScript without output encoding. Request parameter ID is copied into the session (lines 44-47) and then interpolated raw inside a script block at line 69 (window.opener.document.edit_metadata.<ID>.value=...); session attribute filter is written raw into an input value attribute (line 110); ID is written raw into hidden input values (lines 112, 119); both are passed unencoded to the dspace:controlledvocabulary tag (line 138). The values originate from arbitrary request parameters: ControlledVocabularyServlet lines 38-52 read callerUrl, ID and filter from the request and store ID/filter in the session, and are reachable via the public /controlledvocabulary mapping. No escaping function is applied anywhere in the JSP (contrast controlledvocabulary/search.jsp line 56, which escapes the same filter value with Utils.addEntities).
candidates.title: Reflected XSS in JSPUI controlled-vocabulary popup via unencoded request/session parameters (ID, filter)
candidates.trace: Attacker request (e.g. GET /controlledvocabulary/controlledvocabulary.jsp?ID=</script><script>alert(document.domain)</script>, or GET /controlledvocabulary?ID=...&filter=...&callerUrl=...) -> ControlledVocabularyServlet lines 40-52 / controlledvocabulary.jsp lines 45-47 store the raw value in session attributes controlledvocabulary.ID / controlledvocabulary.filter -> raw scriptlet output at line 69 inside a script element and at lines 110, 112, 119 inside HTML attributes -> the HTML parser terminates the script element at the injected </script> (or the attribute at the injected quote) and the attacker script executes in the DSpace origin. A payload such as filter="><script>alert(1)</script> demonstrates the attribute-context variant at line 110.
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-confirmed; no deployed instance was tested. Assumes standard servlet-container JSP handling (JSPs served by the default JSP servlet) and that no external reverse proxy/WAF blocks /controlledvocabulary/*. The exact upstream fix history (whether this or a sibling JSP was the patched file for a given CVE) could not be established from the snapshot.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-79 Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (Cross-site Scripting)

coverage_summary: Coverage: inventory and targeted review of 2028 files (1464 Java, 212 JSP, 97 XML, 18 properties, plus CSS/JS/config). Reviewed core authorization (AuthorizeManager, Bitstream.retrieve), storage (BitstreamStorageManager), discovery/search (SolrServiceImpl, SolrServiceResourceRestrictionPlugin, DiscoverUtility), import/export and packager/crosswalk classes, JSPUI servlets and filters plus public JSPs and web.xml mappings, XMLUI authentication/administrative/discovery/statistics aspects, REST resources and serializers, SWORD/ SWORDv2 authenticators and ingesters, OAI (xoai) classes, Solr LocalHostRestrictionFilter, and LNI/WebDAV classes. Searched for and inspected typical sinks: request.getParameter, sendRedirect, SQL string construction/executeQuery, DocumentBuilderFactory/SAXBuilder/SAXParserFactory, XPath concatenation, Runtime.exec, ObjectInputStream, ZipEntry/new File, getPathInfo, setIgnoreAuthorization, authorizeActionBoolean, and raw JSP expression output; also checked config defaults (dspace.cfg, discovery.xml, web.xml). Not every line of every file was read; generated/web assets (.xsl files, sitemaps) are absent from the snapshot.
limitations: No code was compiled, deployed or executed; all conclusions are static and no exploitation was attempted, so none of the findings are runtime-confirmed.

Only one candidate could be submitted; several additional plausible issues (cc-license.jsp XSS, discovery.jsp spell-check XSS, ItemImport Zip-Slip, open redirects, weak token PRNG, XXE paths, SwordClient SSRF) are documented as leads rather than proven findings.

The snapshot contains no .git history, tests, XSL/sitemap files or upstream diff, so I could not confirm the intended case, the associated CVE/patch, or whether any candidate corresponds to a later fixed version.
Exploitability of the Solr spell-check reflection depends on Apache Solr 4.4 collation behavior that is not present in the snapshot and was not executed.

Deployment-specific protections (reverse proxies, WAFs, custom web.xml overlays) are outside the can?not be seen in this source tree; the selected candidate assumes a standard DSpace JSPUI deployment as configured here.

rejected_leads.lead: Reflected XSS in dspace-jspui/src/main/webapp/submit/cc-license.jsp (license_url parameter written raw into a script string at line 27, page reachable without auth since registered-only maps only the exact /submit path)
rejected_leads.reason: Genuine same-class vulnerability and arguably as severe, but only one candidate is permitted; controlledvocabulary.jsp was selected because it has multiple independent unescaped sinks plus a public servlet that persists the parameters in session, giving the strongest source-evidence chain.

rejected_leads.lead: Potential reflected XSS in dspace-jspui/src/main/webapp/search/discovery.jsp line 199, where the Solr spell-check collation (spellCheckQuery) is printed raw while the same value is escaped in the data-spell attribute
rejected_leads.reason: Attacker control is indirect (depends on the Solr 4.x collation preserving raw query characters), so exploitability could not be proven from the snapshot alone; not selected.

rejected_leads.lead: Zip-Slip in dspace-api/src/main/java/org/dspace/app/itemimport/ItemImport.java lines 515-552 (ZipEntry.getName concatenated into ziptempdir when extracting uploaded archives)
rejected_leads.reason: Real arbitrary-file-write pattern but reachable only from the CLI/admin batch-import endpoint (site-admin), so exposure is lower than an unauthenticated web XSS; not selected under the one-candidate cap.

rejected_leads.lead: Open redirects: ControlledVocabularyServlet.java line 53 (sendRedirect(callerUrl)) and SearchResultLogServlet.java line 71 (sendRedirect(redirectUrl))
rejected_leads.reason: Real but lower-severity issues; both parameters come straight from the request, but reflected XSS has greater impact.

rejected_leads.lead: Weak token generation in dspace-api/src/main/java/org/dspace/core/Utils.java generateBytesKey() using java.util.Random + MD5 for account registration/password-reset tokens and request-item tokens (used by AccountManager and RequestItemManager)
rejected_leads.reason: The token material is MD5(VMID + timestamp + non-crypto-random bytes + counter), so recovering/predicting another user's token is not demonstrable from source evidence alone; kept as an unconfirmed lead.

rejected_leads.lead: XML parsers without hardened configurations (SAXBuilder/DocumentBuilderFactory) reachable from SWORD/METS/WebDAV deposit paths, e.g. dspace-api .../packager/METSManifest.java line 258 and dspace-lni .../dav/DAVResource.java lines 607, 860, 1210, 1678
rejected_leads.reason: XXE is plausible but requires authenticated deposit/WebDAV paths and multiple components to line up; not the strongest verified finding.

rejected_leads.lead: SSRF via the XMLUI SwordClient aspect (dspace-xmlui .../swordclient/SelectTargetAction.java lines 44-95 accepting arbitrary otherUrl and fetching the service document server-side)
rejected_leads.reason: Requires an authenticated user and the SwordClient aspect to be enabled in the sitemap (not present in this snapshot), so exploitation conditions are uncertain.

rejected_leads.lead: Stored XSS candidates via raw metadata rendering (e.g. ItemTag.java lines 533/552/582 raw href values, community-list.jsp short_description output)
rejected_leads.reason: Raw metadata interpolation is real, but the default webui.itemdisplay.default configuration line is commented out in dspace.cfg and the community/collection description sinks need elevated privileges, so reachability/impact is weaker than the selected candidate.

summary: Reviewed the DSpace 4.4 source snapshot (2028 files: 1464 Java, 212 JSP, plus XML/config/JS) across dspace-api, dspace-jspui, dspace-xmlui, dspace-rest, dspace-sword/swordv2, dspace-oai, dspace-solr, dspace-lni and dspace-services, tracing web-reachable input to sinks. Strongest source-provable issue: reflected XSS in the JSPUI controlled-vocabulary popup. Request parameters (ID, filter) are stored verbatim in the session by the public ControlledVocabularyServlet and by controlledvocabulary.jsp, then written unencoded into a script block and into HTML attribute values in controlledvocabulary.jsp, allowing markup/script breakout in the DSpace origin for any unauthenticated victim who follows a crafted URL. Several other genuine leads exist (second JSPUI reflected XSS in submit/cc-license.jsp, possible spell-check XSS in search/discovery.jsp, Zip-Slip in ItemImport, open redirects, weak token PRNG, XML parser XXE paths) but only one candidate is allowed. Nothing was executed or runtime-confirmed.
